title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ORTHODONTIC DIAGNOSIS: HISTORY, CHATBOT TECHNOLOGY, DIAGNOSTIC FOUNDATIONS, AND ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS
Digital twin technology in dentistry: Applications, challenges, and future perspectives in precision oral healthcare
abstract: Background Digital twin technology creates virtual replicas enabling real-time monitoring, simulation, and predictive analysis. Whilst extensively explored in medical disciplines, its integration in dentistry remains emerging. Complex anatomical structures, individualised treatment requirements, and precision demands position digital twin technology as promising for enhancing clinical outcomes and patient care. Aim This review examines current applications of digital twin technology in dentistry, identifies associated benefits and challenges, and explores future directions for research and practice. Method A comprehensive narrative review searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore for articles published between 2015 and 2026. Search terms included combinations of "digital twin", "virtual twin", "virtual patient model", "digital replica", "dentistry", "oral health", and related dental specialty terms, combined using Boolean operators. Articles focusing on digital twin applications, implementation strategies, technological frameworks, and clinical outcomes were included. Results Digital twin technology demonstrates diverse applications across orthodontics, prosthodontics, oral surgery, endodontics, and periodontics. Key applications include treatment planning, surgical simulation, prosthesis design, outcome prediction, and patient education. The technology integrates three-dimensional imaging, intraoral scanning, electronic health records, and biomechanical simulations to create comprehensive virtual representations. Where genuine bidirectional digital twin frameworks are implemented, benefits include enhanced precision, reduced treatment time, improved outcomes, and personalised care. However, challenges related to data integration, computational requirements, costs, and standardisation persist. Conclusion Digital twin technology holds substantial promise for advancing dental practice through improved treatment planning, enhanced precision, and personalised care. As technological infrastructure develops and integration challenges are addressed, applications are expected to expand significantly, transforming clinical workflows and elevating standards. However, the current evidence base remains largely preliminary, and large-scale clinical validation is needed before definitive conclusions can be drawn.
authors: David Bamidele Olawade; Priscillia C. Fidelis; Olabanke Florence Olawuyi; Rosemary Olasilola; Babajide David Makanjuola; John Oluwatosin Alabi

title: Overview of Persistent Inter-Professional Rivalry Within the Laboratory Medicine Practice Domain of Tertiary Healthcare Institutions in Nigeria: A Narrative Review
abstract: The persistent inter-professional rivalry within the laboratory medicine practice domain of Nigerian tertiary healthcare institutions constitutes a systemic crisis that undermines diagnostic accuracy, jeopardizes patient safety, and disrupts healthcare delivery. This longstanding conflict between the Medical Laboratory Scientists (MLS) and the laboratory-based physicians (Clinical Pathologists) centers mainly on operational independence, leadership in clinical laboratories, and statutory boundaries. This review examines the historical, legal, educational, and socio-political causes of this rivalry in Nigerian tertiary healthcare settings. Historically, laboratory medicine practice functions shifted from physician-led to specialized, autonomous scientific roles, leading to overlapping claims over laboratory and clinical consultation domains. Conflicting laws—such as the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) Practitioners Act and the Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria (MLSCN) Act—have created parallel regulatory frameworks, resulting in ongoing legal disputes at the National Industrial Court. These dynamics foster operational silos, strikes, and diagnostic errors, often causing preventable misdiagnoses. To transform this rivalry into collaborative clinical efforts, the article recommends a comprehensive approach that includes legislative reforms, separation of administrative and clinical roles, formal interprofessional education in training, and joint governance boards in tertiary healthcare settings. Ultimately, resolving this conflict is vital to achieving international standards and protecting Nigerian patient care from interprofessional conflicts.
authors: Collins Amadi; Roy Amadi; Sasha Amadi; Elena Amadi; Comfort John

title: Patients’ Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Dental Practice: A Cross-Sectional Study from Romania
abstract: Background/Objectives: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into dental practice is reshaping clinical workflows, administrative processes, and, increasingly, the patient experience and the doctor–patient relationship. While prior research has documented the attitudes of clinicians and practice managers, the perspective of the patient remains comparatively underexplored. This study examined how dental patients perceive AI integration and digital tools across the dental care pathway, together with the associated implications for data security, cost, and the human dimension of care. Methods: A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study was conducted among 200 dental patients in Bucharest, Romania, and the surrounding region. The instrument assessed perceived difficulty and availability regarding digital technology, current use of digital tools, demographic and educational characteristics (age, gender, practice environment, educational level), and two attitudinal dimensions, namely digital prudence and concern for technological sustainability, across five subdomains of the dental care pathway: scheduling, diagnosis, treatment planning, feedback, and follow-up (dispensarization). Responses were analyzed using non-parametric tests and exploratory principal component analysis with internal-consistency validation. Results: Patients expressed moderate-to-high interest in AI support during the diagnostic (median = 3.3, IQR = 2.7–3.9) and feedback (median = 3.11, IQR = 2.78–3.67) stages and the lowest interest in scheduling (median = 2.7, IQR = 2.0–3.3). A marked level of digital prudence was observed (median = 3.24, IQR = 2.82–3.61), reflecting concerns about data security, automation, and a possible weakening of the clinician–patient bond. Younger and academically educated patients reported lower perceived difficulty, higher availability, and greater current use of digital tools (all p ≤ 0.001); counterintuitively, the same patients scored significantly higher on digital prudence (Spearman’s ρ = −0.260, p < 0.001). Greater familiarity with digital tools was therefore accompanied by a more critical awareness of their informational risks rather than by uncritical acceptance. Conclusions: Dental patients approach AI through a dual lens of openness and informed caution, welcoming efficiency gains in the clinical and continuity-of-care stages while voicing measured concerns about data security, affordability, and the preservation of human contact. To interpret this profile, we propose two conceptual contributions: a mapping of patient needs onto Maslow’s hierarchy in the context of AI-mediated care and the Informational VUCA framework, which characterizes the volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity that patients face when navigating AI-generated information. The findings point to a clear practical agenda of transparent communication, robust data governance, and education strategies adapted to patients’ educational and demographic profiles, so that AI-enhanced workflows strengthen rather than erode the doctor–patient relationship.
authors: Alin Flavius Cozmescu; Ana Cernega; Andreea Cristiana Didilescu; Marina Meleșcanu Imre; Cristian Funieru; Silviu-Mirel Pițuru

title: Perception of Special Needs Dentistry Amongst Allied Dental Professionals in Australia
abstract: OBJECTIVE: In Australia, Dental Therapists (DTs), Dental Hygienists (DHs) and Oral Health Therapists (OHTs) encounter Special Needs (SN) patients in their clinical practice. This study investigates their perception, training, working experience and referral patterns within Special Needs Dentistry (SND). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Paper-based questionnaire was distributed to a systematically selected sample of 1000 registered DHs, DTs and OHTs who were members of professional bodies in Australia. Respondents were included irrespective of age, gender, length of working experience and country of graduation. Data analysis consisted of Chi-squared regression analysis (p < 0.05) using IBM SPSS Windows Version 29.0 (Melbourne, Victoria, Australia). RESULTS: A response rate of 49.8% (215 DTs, 107 DHs and 163 OHTs) was obtained. A significantly larger proportion of OHTs (59.5%) was aware of SND as a specialty compared to DHs (45%) and DTs (41.9%) (p < 0.05) and hence OHTs referred to SND specialists more often than other groups. In addition, 73.6% of OHTs, 63.6% of DHs and 40% of DTs had both didactic and clinical training in SND (p < 0.05). All the categories stated lack of training and continuing professional development (CPD) in SND as the main reasons for not treating SN patients. They therefore expressed interest in attending related CPD training (OHTs: 90.2%, DHs: 88.8% and DTs: 88.3%). CONCLUSIONS: OHTs demonstrated greater awareness, training, working experience and referral in SND than DHs and DTs; however, training gaps across all groups highlight the need for strengthened undergraduate education and accessible CPD in SND. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Understanding the perception of allied dental professionals regarding SND is crucial for improving access to and the quality of care for patients with special needs. Prior research has highlighted gaps in training and confidence levels amongst general practitioners; however, little is known about the perspectives of allied professionals. This study provides valuable insights into their awareness, perceived roles and educational needs, emphasizing the importance of inclusive team-based care.
authors: Jessica Francis; Gelsomina L. Borromeo

title: Next-generation microneedle patches for transdermal therapeutics and diagnostics
abstract: Microneedle patches (MNPs) have emerged as versatile platforms for minimally invasive transdermal drug delivery, biosensing, and point-of-care diagnostics by transiently breaching the stratum corneum while minimizing pain and tissue damage. Recent advances in biomaterials, microfabrication, additive manufacturing, and bioelectronics have expanded MNP functionality beyond drug delivery to include controlled therapeutic release, interstitial fluid sampling, wearable biosensing, and closed-loop therapeutic systems. However, despite substantial technological progress, clinical translation remains constrained by challenges related to manufacturing scalability, device reproducibility, standardized characterization, quality assurance, regulatory approval, and commercialization. Unlike previous reviews that primarily emphasize microneedle classifications or material platforms, this review provides a critical translational perspective by integrating materials science, engineering, manufacturing, biosensing, and regulatory considerations into a unified framework. Major fabrication strategies, material platforms, and characterization methods are systematically compared with respect to mechanical performance, manufacturability, reproducibility, and clinical applicability. Current therapeutic and diagnostic applications are critically evaluated alongside the key barriers to industrial production and regulatory implementation. Emerging opportunities, including smart biosensing, stimuli-responsive materials, additive manufacturing, and closed-loop therapeutic systems, are also discussed. By highlighting the factors that govern technology readiness and clinical implementation, this review provides practical insights for accelerating the development and commercialization of next-generation microneedle platforms for drug delivery, biosensing, vaccination, and precision medicine.
authors: Tsung‐Hsien Chen; Ming‐Tse Hsu; Kun-Hua Lee; Riya Karmakar; Arvind Mukundan; Sangamithirai Sridharan Kuzhali; Chu‐Kuang Chou; Wen-Shou Lin; Hsiang‐Chen Wang

title: Evaluation of LLMs for Automated Dental-to-Medical Consult Letter Generation: Comparative Study
abstract: INTRODUCTION AND AIMS: For dental patients with systemic diseases, multidisciplinary care via referral letters is essential for clinical safety. This study evaluated the clinical feasibility and quality of dental-to-medical referral letters generated by Large Language Models (LLMs). METHODS: Using 153 paired datasets, three LLMs - Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-5 and MedGemma - generated referral letters via a standardised prompting framework. Two dental clinicians performed a blinded assessment across nine sub-criteria covering content, style and correctness. GPT-5 also performed an automated evaluation. Statistical significance was analysed using Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction. RESULTS: In the human clinical evaluation, Gemini-2.5-Pro achieved the highest overall performance (TOTAL mean SCORE: 2.9487 with a bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI] of 2.9345-2.9606), significantly outperforming GPT-5 (2.8818 with 95% CI of 2.8613-2.9008) and MedGemma (2.8613 with 95% CI of 2.8338-2.8865) (P < .05). While GPT-5 showed high clarity in systemic problem descriptions, MedGemma excelled in structural adherence. The overall performance difference between GPT-5 and MedGemma was not statistically significant (P = .3519). Inter-rater reliability was strong in the prompt search dataset (QWK: 0.7175) but lower in the independent test dataset (QWK: 0.1505), reflecting the subjective nature of clinical document assessment; therefore, final human scores were reported as average ratings from two blinded clinicians with bootstrap confidence intervals. Notably, GPT-5's self-evaluation results deviated from human judgment, exhibiting potential model-based bias. CONCLUSION: This preliminary study suggests the potential of Gemini-2.5-Pro for automated consult letter generation, though the low test-set inter-rater reliability (QWK: 0.1505) highlights the subjective complexity of clinical text. To integrate these assistive prototypes into routine clinical application, more systematic studies are required. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Integrating LLMs offers a promising approach to assisting with dental-to-medical referrals, presenting a potential future benefit of reducing administrative workloads and enabling healthcare providers to focus on safe, empathetic patient care.
authors: Dareen Eom; Kyeol Koh; Howon Chung; Kwangsoo Kim; Sang Hwa Lee

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A DECISION-SUPPORT TOOL FOR MATERIAL SELECTION IN PROSTHODONTICS: AN ANALYTICAL REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE
abstract: Background. The rapid development of digital dentistry and artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding the range of technologies available for diagnosis, treatment planning, prosthetic design, and outcome prediction. Material selection remains a clinically important component of prosthodontic treatment because the choice of restorative material must account for mechanical, functional, biological, and esthetic requirements. Aim. To analyze recent literature on the application of AI in prosthodontics, with particular attention to its potential role in supporting restorative material selection, integrating clinical and digital parameters, predicting prosthetic outcomes, and personalizing treatment planning. Materials and methods. A narrative analytical review was developed from literature published during seven completed calendar years (January 2019–December 2025). Relevant publications were identified in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and NCBI resources using combinations of terms related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, prosthodontics, dental materials, CAD/CAM, crowns, dental prostheses, occlusion, and treatment outcomes. Publications were thematically analyzed according to AI application, type of prosthodontic task, data source, clinical purpose, reported outcomes, and limitations. Results. The reviewed literature demonstrates that AI is increasingly applied in prosthodontic diagnostics, treatment planning, automated crown design, finish-line detection, occlusal assessment, prediction of prosthetic outcomes, and digital workflows. AI-assisted CAD systems have shown potential to improve design efficiency and, in selected studies, achieve clinically acceptable crown fit. However, the evidence remains heterogeneous with substantial differences in datasets, algorithms, validation procedures, and outcome measures. Direct evidence supporting independently validated AI systems for individualized restorative material selection remains limited. Current evidence therefore supports the use of AI primarily as a clinical decision-support tool rather than as an autonomous system for material selection. Conclusions. AI has considerable potential to support individualized material selection and prosthodontic treatment planning by integrating multiple clinical and digital parameters. At the same time, current evidence does not support treating AI as an autonomous replacement for professional clinical judgment. Direct validation of AI systems specifically designed to select restorative materials remains limited, and many predictive models require stronger external validation and prospective clinical evaluation. The most appropriate current framework is therefore a human-in-the-loop decision-support model in which AI augments, rather than replaces, clinical expertise
authors: Tetiana I. Dzetsiukh

title: DentalGEN: a large-scale controllable generative AI framework for automated dental crown restoration
abstract: Dental crown restoration addresses a global public health burden, yet is constrained by a slow, variable, and labor-intensive manual design process that limits access to high-quality treatment. Here we introduce DentalGEN, a large-scale controllable generative artificial intelligence framework for automated dental crown restoration. DentalGEN is the first framework capable of designing a patient-specific crown while simultaneously satisfying morphological, functional, and aesthetic criteria. Its core is a novel multi-view diffusion model that leverages explicit control mechanisms to incorporate clinical constraints directly within the generative process. This approach enables the integrated synthesis of view-consistent geometry and texture, achieving a level of precision and integration unattainable with prior automated methods. Evaluated on the largest reported multi-center dataset, DentalGEN’s designs achieved clinical scores statistically equivalent to those of human experts in blinded assessments, while outperforming state-of-the-art methods by 70% in Hausdorff Distance. Furthermore, a clinical proof-of-concept study demonstrated the feasibility of integrating DentalGEN into a supervised scan-design-manufacture paradigm, reducing active design time by over 90%. DentalGEN represents a crucial step in bridging the translational gap for generative AI in dental restoration, paving the way for more accessible, accurate, and efficient dental care.
authors: Jiamin Wu; Ying Liu; Yanning Chen; Yuqiang Zhang; Jiaying Gu; Yuan Liu; Mengxun Li; Wenping Wang; Yuanfei Fu; Zhiming Cui; James Kit Hon Tsoi; Dinggang G. Shen

title: The use of Artificial Intelligence in Dentistry: Applications, challenges, and future perspectives
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence [AI] has enhanced contemporary dental practice by providing advanced tools for diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient management. Objective: This narrative review examines the current applications of AI in dentistry, evaluates its diagnostic efficacy, identifies challenges for clinical implementation, and discusses future perspectives. Methods: A narrative literature review was conducted by searching PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, and LILACS for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Observational studies randomized clinical trials, systematic reviews, and methodological studies were included. DeCS/MeSH descriptors were combined using the Boolean operators AND and OR. Study selection was purposive, prioritizing recent publications with higher methodological quality and scientific relevance. Results: AI demonstrated high accuracy in detecting dental caries, periapical lesions, periodontal diseases, and other oral conditions. Applications span all dental specialties, including radiology, endodontics, orthodontics, periodontics, and oral and maxillofacial surgery. Despite these advancements, significant barriers persist, including ethical concerns regarding patient privacy, the need for rigorous clinical validation, and integration into existing clinical workflows. AI should be considered a complementary tool that enhances clinician capabilities rather than a substitute for clinical judgment. The future of dentistry will involve the integration of explainable AI systems, federated learning for data protection, and digital education for the dental workforce. Conclusion: AI holds transformative potential to improve access, quality, and efficiency in dental care, provided it is implemented with methodological rigor, continuous human oversight, and appropriate ethical considerations.
authors: Glayson Pereira Vitor

title: Terahertz Antenna Design for Biomedical Sensing and Imaging
abstract: Background/objectives: Research in terahertz (THz) frequency range has accelerated, bridging the gap between microwave and infrared technologies, in response to the increasing demand for quicker data transmission, improved image resolution, and effective biomedical diagnostics. The non-ionizing nature of the THz band makes it highly suitable for high-resolution imaging and noninvasive biomedical sensing. The choice of substrate, however, significantly impacts on THz antenna performance, affecting radiation efficiency, bandwidth, and biocompatibility. This study aims to construct and optimize microstrip patch antennas operating at 1 THz to determine which substrate is best suited for biological sensing and imaging applications. This study also aims to develop a comparative understanding of the impact of substrate dielectric characteristics on antenna performance and their suitability for integration into sixth-generation (6G)-enabled healthcare systems. Methods: CST Microwave Studio was used to model and simulate several THz microstrip patch antennas. A 50-Ω waveguide port was used to excite each antenna, and open boundary conditions were used to simulate free-space propagation. Several substrate materials, such as polyimide, FR4, Rogers RT/Duroid 5880, gallium arsenide (GaAs), and silicon arsenide (SiAs), were selected for comparative analysis of THz antenna performance. To assess return loss, gain, directivity, bandwidth, and radiation efficiency, frequency sweeps were conducted over 0.5–1.5 THz. Finding the substrate material with the best trade-offs between electrical and biological compatibility was the primary goal of the comparative investigation. Results: According to simulation data, polyimide and Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrates outperformed FR4, GaAs, and SiAs in terms of antenna performance. With gain values of approximately 5 dBi at 1 THz, these materials demonstrated improved radiation efficiency, a wider impedance bandwidth, and minimum return loss (<−30 dB). In on-body designs, polyimide offers additional benefits, such as flexibility, low dielectric loss, and consistent responsiveness, making it particularly suitable for wearable biomedical devices. The investigation confirmed that impedance matching and the overall radiation behavior are significantly influenced by the substrate’s dielectric constant and loss tangent. The findings indicate the promise of THz antennas for high-speed wireless communication, noninvasive diagnosis, and real-time biological sensing in healthcare settings. Conclusions: This study offers a methodical comparison of THz patch antennas made of various substrate materials for biomedical imaging and sensing. According to the results, polyimide and Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 are the most effective substrates because they provide the best possible balance of biocompatibility, wide bandwidth, and high gain. The integration of these materials into future implantable and wearable medical systems based on THz shows excellent promise. For 6G communication-enabled healthcare networks and next-generation biomedical equipment, the study advances the creation of high-performance antennas. Future work includes exploring flexible and miniature antenna topologies, experimental validation of the proposed designs, and evaluating real-time performance in biological environments.
authors: Mandeep Singh; Simranjit Singh; Simarpreet Kaur

title: Clinical Reasoning: A 60-Year-Old Woman With Fever, Headache, Diplopia, and Unilateral Periorbital Swelling
abstract: Evaluating delayed vascular complications after a focal cranial infection can be diagnostically challenging. In this case, a 60-year-old woman with approximately 1 month of recurrent gingival swelling and pain later developed fever and headache, followed by horizontal diplopia and progressive unilateral periorbital swelling. Examination showed a left abduction deficit and conjunctival chemosis. Cerebral angiography obtained during evaluation demonstrated severe narrowing of the cavernous segment of the internal carotid artery. Although the patient improved clinically after antimicrobial therapy, routine follow-up imaging 1 year later revealed a new vascular lesion at the site of the prior arterial abnormality. This case highlights the importance of interval neurovascular follow-up imaging when cavernous internal carotid artery abnormalities are identified during the initial presentation of febrile ophthalmoplegia.
authors: Naijimiding Rexiati; Naijimiding Rexiati; Shihao Jiang; Aximujiang Axier; Nizhamidingjiang Rexiati; Nizhamidingjiang Rexiati; Riqing Su; Zengliang Wang; Pahaerding Balatiniyazi; Aisha Maimaitili

title: Effects of Dental Noise on Dentists’ Performance and Stress Responses: A Randomized Crossover Trial
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of continuous noise generated during dental treatment on dentists' performance and stress responses. METHODS: This study involved a questionnaire survey and an experimental investigation. The questionnaire survey was conducted with 44 dentists to assess dental noise-related subjective burden and noise sources perceived as the most uncomfortable. In the experimental phase, a randomized crossover trial was performed with 11 participants under silent and noisy conditions. Work performance was evaluated using the total number of calculations (work volume) and error rates in the Uchida-Kraepelin test. Saliva samples were collected before, during, and after the test, and salivary alpha-amylase (sAA), chromogranin A (CgA), and secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) levels were measured to assess stress responses. RESULTS: In the questionnaire survey, clinical noise was perceived as uncomfortable by 93.2% of dentists, with the extraoral suction unit being identified as the most unpleasant device (equivalent continuous noise level: 91.7 ± 0.6 dBA). In the randomized crossover trial, work volume in the Uchida-Kraepelin test significantly decreased, and the error rates significantly increased, under the noisy condition. With respect to salivary stress markers, sAA levels were significantly higher under the noisy condition, and sIgA levels were significantly increased. By contrast, CgA levels did not significantly differ between the conditions. Furthermore, sAA levels were significantly correlated with work performance. CONCLUSIONS: Dental noise reduced dentists' performance and elicited stress responses. These findings highlight the need for noise mitigation and occupational stress management strategies in dental practice.
authors: Daisuke Kido; Sayaka Katagiri; Ayako Tanaka; Sachi Umemori; Koji Mizutani; Hiroshi Nitta

title: Prospects for respiratory training with immersive technologies and biofeedback in patients of outpatient dental practice
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of structured respiratory training using virtual reality (VR) and biofeedback for reducing psychophysiological tension in patients of outpatient dental practice. Thirty-four patients were enrolled in this pilot randomised study and allocated to a main group (training with VR and biofeedback, n=17) and a comparison group (n=17). In the main group, breathing awareness increased from 35.8±7.5 to 41.4±9.0 points (p=0.052 by the sign test and p=0.011 by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test) and relaxation self-efficacy increased from 4.8±3.6 to 7.0±3.5 points (p=0.043 by the sign test and p=0.006 by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Between-group comparison of changes showed a statistically significant advantage of VR-assisted training for the gain in breathing awareness (p=0.038 by the Mann–Whitney U-test); no between-group difference was found for relaxation self-efficacy (p=0.092). The findings suggest that a single session of respiratory training with immersive technologies and biofeedback promotes the development of breathing self-regulation skills. Given the sample size, the single-session design and the use of non-validated scales, these data are preliminary and require confirmation in larger studies assessing anxiety, autonomic measures and treatment adherence.
