title: Digital Health Revolution in Saudi Arabia: A Narrative Review of Healthcare Transformation
abstract: Digital transformation (DT) is a strategic priority for healthcare systems seeking to improve the quality of care, patient safety, and operational efficiency. In Saudi Arabia, DT is central to Vision 2030; however, evidence regarding its effects on healthcare quality and safety remains dispersed across technologies and healthcare settings. This narrative review aimed to examine the impact of digital transformation on healthcare quality and patient safety in Saudi Arabia and to identify the principal implementation facilitators, barriers, and policy implications. A structured narrative literature search was conducted for publications from January 2010 to March 2026 using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, the Saudi Digital Library, and relevant Saudi governmental and policy documents. In total, 64 peer-reviewed studies, reviews, reports, and policy documents addressing digital health initiatives and outcomes related to quality, safety, efficiency, or patient experience were included. Evidence was synthesized thematically, focusing on electronic health records, digital prescribing, online appointment systems, clinical and pharmacy automation, claims and financial analytics, telemedicine, governance, and workforce factors. The reviewed evidence indicates that Electronic Health Record (EHRs), computerized provider order entry, e-prescribing, barcode-supported medication systems, telemedicine, digital appointment platforms, and automated workflows can improve access to care, documentation, care coordination, medication safety, workflow efficiency, and patient experience. However, the benefits of DT are constrained by fragmented infrastructure, limited interoperability, workforce resistance, insufficient digital literacy, funding limitations, and unclear or fragmented governance and regulatory arrangements. In conclusion, digital transformation has substantial potential to enhance healthcare quality and patient safety in Saudi Arabia. Achieving these benefits requires context-sensitive implementation, interoperable systems, strong governance, sustained investment in infrastructure and workforce capacity, and effective leadership and change-management strategies aligned with Vision 2030.
authors: Mahmoud Abdel Hameed Shahin

title: Integrating artificial intelligence into medical laboratories: A structured implementation framework
abstract: This article presents a structured framework for integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into medical laboratory workflows. As laboratories face increasing demands, workforce shortages, and technological complexity, AI offers promising solutions to enhance efficiency, diagnostic accuracy, and predictive capabilities. The paper outlines key benefits of AI, including automation, quality assurance, and administrative optimization, while also addressing critical challenges such as bias, legal and ethical concerns, workforce disruption, and over-reliance on automated systems. A multi-level implementation strategy is proposed, spanning international, national, and organizational domains, with emphasis on standards, guidelines, training, and oversight. Importantly, the article underscores that AI is a supportive tool, not a replacement for laboratory professionals, whose expertise remains essential for validation and interpretation. The framework aims to guide responsible AI adoption while safeguarding quality and patient safety.
authors: Avi Peretz; Hanoch Goldshmidt; Sari Peretz; Marielle Kaplan; Orna Schwartz; Ronit Marco; Maya Azrad

title: Agentic systems in computational pathology: architectures, evidence, and translational challenges
abstract: BACKGROUND: Digital pathology supports whole-slide imaging, remote review, and computational analysis. Most pathology AI systems, however, remain restricted to predefined tasks. Agentic architectures coordinate perception models, language-based reasoning, external tools, and feedback-dependent actions, but their clinical evidence is derived mainly from retrospective benchmarks and research prototypes. MAIN BODY: We review agentic systems in computational pathology using an operational taxonomy based on dynamic control flow, inference-time tool selection, and knowledge integration. We assess architectures, enabling technologies, and applications in diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic support. Reported gains are difficult to attribute to agentic organization because studies differ in backbones, training data, and inference budgets. We therefore emphasize validation scope, computational cost, workflow integration, hallucination and security risks, regulatory requirements, patient preferences, and the conditions under which specialist non-agentic models remain preferable. CONCLUSIONS: Agentic architectures have established technical feasibility, but not clinical benefit. Translation should prioritize verifiable tasks, matched comparisons, prospective and external validation, lifecycle governance, and interfaces that preserve pathologist oversight.
authors: Xinyu Lu; Qiankun Li; Yakun Gao; Dong Wei; Mengyao Lyu; Siyuan Ma; Jinyue Li; Yufeng Wu; Linghan Cai; Tianyi Zhang; Shangqing Lyu; Zeyu Liu; Hui Liu; Ting Gang Luo

title: The Algorithmic Virologist: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Across Viral Detection, Diagnosis, Surveillance, Prediction, and Therapeutics
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly revolutionizing medical virology, yet its applications remain fragmented, ranging from virus detection and clinical diagnosis to epidemiological prediction, variant monitoring, and treatment development. This review provides a comprehensive overview of AI principles, from basic genomic biology and drug discovery to clinical physiology, and proposes the generation of integrated knowledge, under human supervision, through an "algorithmic virologist" as a conceptual framework to bridge these currently disparate fields. The research assesses deep learning, machine learning, hybrid computational approaches and recent multimodal and generative AI systems with explicit emphasis on their biological validity, diagnostic performance, generalizability, interpretability and translational ability. Current evidence shows that AI can improve reference-free detection of viral sequences, facilitate and inform multimodal clinical diagnosis, combine genomic and epidemiological signals for outbreak and variant prediction, speed up anti-viral target identification and virtual screening and help optimize therapeutics. Yet the review also points out an enduring divide – between computational prowess and real-world clinical utility. Heterogeneous and geographically non-representative datasets, small reference databases of viruses, lack of external and prospective validation, algorithmic black-boxing, potential model drift due to viral and epidemiological changes over time, inadequate interoperability with clinical technologies or other data in use at the bedside or by public health practitioners (and inadequate access at scale) are major barriers to implementation. Consequently, the study proposes that the progress that follows cannot be based on predictive accuracy alone but also needs to keep in mind biological plausibility, external and temporal validity, assessment of uncertainty, explainability; reproducibility; equity and measurable clinical or public-health benefit. Accordingly, it is proposed that the algorithmic virologist is not just a medicine for human knowledge, but an integrated computer ecosystem that links detection, diagnosis, characterization, prediction, monitoring, therapeutic discovery, therapeutic improvement, and continuous verification. Responsibly integrated AI, the review concludes, could facilitate a transition from largely reactive to predictive and anticipatory virology, if they are biologically grounded algorithmic innovations that are experimentally validated, clinically accountable and meaningfully overseen by humans.
authors: Saif Jabbar Yasir

title: Comprehensive Analysis of Laboratory Automation Systems in Evaluating Efficiency, Accuracy, and Workflow Optimization in Diagnostic Testing Through Critical Review
abstract: The given paper is meant to discuss laboratory automation systems in greater detail. It is from the point of view of efficiency, accuracy, and how the processes can be automated. The essence of the study is to critically examine different laboratory automation systems and their respective functions. These components make up the various systems, as well as how the systems affect laboratory operations. A detailed analysis weighs multiple critical factors, including cost-effectiveness, implementation, and potential outcomes. The results of this laboratory automation study demonstrate this invention's significance in enhancing existing diagnostic efficiency, achieving diagnostic accuracy, simplifying workflow processes with eased workflow, and enhancing patient care outcomes.
authors: Hassan Mosa Ahmed Khobrani; Yousef Mutad Atqa Alharbi; Mohmmed Abdullah Alqahtani; Hassan Nasser Abdullah Alqahtani

title: The Cyber-Physical Attack Surface of Legacy Scada Networks: A Systematic Review of Vulnerabilities, Threats, and Detection Gaps in Critical Infrastructure
abstract: Legacy Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) networks remain the operational backbone of the electric power, water treatment, and oil-and-gas sectors, yet they were engineered in an era that prioritized deterministic availability and physical safety over information security. The progressive convergence of information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) has dissolved the air gaps that once isolated these systems, exposing an attack surface for which their aging protocol stacks were never designed. Field-level communication standards such as Modbus and DNP3 typically transmit control directives without encryption, authentication, or message integrity, allowing an adversary who reaches the network to forge, replay, or manipulate commands at will. The defining hazard of this domain is the cyber-physical attack, in which a purely digital intrusion is translated into tangible physical damage, service disruption, or threats to human life. Against this class of threat, conventional signature- and rule-based intrusion detection is structurally inadequate, missing novel and stealthy manipulations while generating unsustainable false-alarm volumes. This review systematically synthesizes the vulnerability landscape, a taxonomy of cyber-physical threats, landmark incidents including Stuxnet, the 2015 Ukrainian grid attack, TRITON, and Maroochy, the protocol-level weaknesses of legacy assets, and the resulting detection gap. Drawing together the industrial-control and applied cybersecurity literature, it argues that intelligent behavioural anomaly detection offers the most credible path toward resilient protection of critical infrastructure
authors: Chukwunenye Amadi

title: Digital technology, healthcare delivery, and patient satisfaction: The moderating effect of innovation technology on the ghanaian health sector
abstract: Though there has been increased development of health delivery in the health sector across the world, nevertheless, there is little indication of how this has improved patient satisfaction in Ghanaian health services. The improvement of health services is hinges on easy retrieval of patient records, and the ability of the health professional to study the history of the patient over some time, and how they are responding to medication: This requires the improvement of digital technology such as the blockchain system, which allow users to follow the thread of information. Artificial Intelligence heavily depends on the mining of data to be effective, and so is health care services. There have been many interventions by the Ghanaian Government to improve the health service through digital technology, such as creating centralized healthcare data systems and the blockchain system. However, measuring the level of this introduction on patient satisfaction is yet to be studied. This research tries to identify how this satisfaction is realized based on the healthcare personnel who have direct contact with the patients. The research findings indicate that the healthcare service has greatly improved with the introduction of digital services in both private and public health services, and it significantly impacts patient and doctor relationships. In addition, the research finding indicates that some barriers needs to be addressed with to facilitate the introduction of these new digital technology. The research recommends that the government need focus on the improvement of the digitization of health services, and facilitate the replacement of out datated systems in the health care services.
authors: Joseph Lanton Adjei Mensah
venue: Journal of Business & Retail Management Research

title: Predictive Analytics in Banking: Regulatory Reporting, Supervision, and Portfolio Oversight, Advances and Future Opportunities
abstract: Predictive analytics has moved from a peripheral experimental capability to a central instrument in how banks report to regulators, how supervisors monitor systemic and idiosyncratic risk, and how institutions oversee the health of their portfolios. This paper surveys the state of the art across three interlocking domains (regulatory reporting, prudential supervision, and portfolio oversight) and articulates a forward-looking research agenda. We trace the technical lineage from classical statistical credit models such as discriminant analysis and structural default frameworks to contemporary machine-learning ensembles, and we situate these methods within the regulatory architecture of the Basel framework, IFRS 9 expected credit loss provisioning, BCBS 239 risk-data aggregation principles, and supervisory model-risk expectations. We synthesise advances in seven application clusters: credit and default prediction, expected credit loss estimation, stress testing, RegTech and SupTech automated reporting, anti-money-laundering and fraud analytics, portfolio monitoring and early-warning systems, and explainability and model risk. A structured table maps techniques to supervisory use cases. We then examine open challenges that constrain deployment: fragmented and low-quality data, the tension between predictive accuracy and interpretability under regulatory scrutiny, procyclicality risks embedded in point-in-time forecasts, model-risk governance, and accountability for automated decisions. Finally, we set out future opportunities spanning privacy-preserving supervisory analytics, machine-readable regulation, causal and stress-aware modelling, and human-in-the-loop governance. We argue that the marginal value of predictive analytics in banking now depends less on raw algorithmic performance and more on governance, data infrastructure, and the credibility of models under supervisory challenge.
authors: Ifeanyichukwu Jeffrey Okwesa; Uchechi Mary-Linda Unamma; Funmilayo Ashore-Onisemo; Serif Oyindamola Oyesiji

title: Advances In NLP-Driven Analytics for Automated Detection of Regulatory Liabilities in High-Volume Contracts
abstract: Contract portfolios at large enterprises now routinely exceed tens of thousands of active agreements, and the regulatory obligations attaching to those agreements have multiplied faster than legal review capacity. In 2025 this gap became acute: the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) became applicable on 17 January without a transition period, forcing thousands of financial entities into large-scale contract remediation, while the general-purpose AI obligations of the EU AI Act took effect on 2 August. Both events created demand for systems that can read an entire contract portfolio and flag, with evidence, where regulatory liability exists. This paper reviews the state of natural language processing for automated regulatory liability detection as of the end of 2025 and sets out a layered architecture for production deployment. Regulatory liability detection is distinguished here from the better-studied task of clause extraction, on the argument that the former is a normative verification problem requiring a rule base, an evidence retrieval mechanism, and an adjudication step, rather than a span-labelling problem. Four technical shifts that reshaped the field during 2025 are surveyed: the maturation of long-context models beyond the length of most commercial contracts, the emergence of legal-specific retrieval evaluation, the arrival of explicit reasoning models capable of rule-grounded justification, and the closing but still material gap between proprietary and open-weight models on clause-level risk identification. Evidence is also drawn from compliance analytics research in financial audit, cybersecurity governance, critical infrastructure protection, procurement, supply chain assurance, payments, pharmaceutical regulation, aviation safety oversight, and enterprise systems engineering, on the argument that the design problems in regulatory liability detection are not confined to legal NLP and that adjacent literatures have already resolved several of them. A metric suite appropriate to the asymmetric cost structure of compliance work is then set out, in which a missed mandatory clause is not commensurate with a false alarm, and the F1 scores dominant in the literature are argued to be a poor proxy for deployment value. The paper closes on a reflexive governance question specific to this application: a system that classifies legal risk may itself fall within the scope of the regulation it is deployed to manage.

title: Organ-on-a-chip platforms for disease modeling and in vitro diagnostic applications
abstract: Organ-on-a-Chip (OoC) systems, as microphysiological models integrating microfluidic engineering, 3D tissue construction, and sensing technologies, can faithfully recapitulate the barrier functions, dynamic microenvironments, and inter-tissue crosstalk of human organs. They effectively address the inherent limitations of traditional 2D cell cultures and animal models in in vitro diagnostics (IVD), offering a novel avenue to tackle the high failure rate of candidate drugs and biomarkers in clinical translation. This review systematically summarizes the technological advances and application practices of OoC in the IVD field, covering core construction technologies (microfluidic regulation, cell and tissue engineering, material innovation), the integrated optimization of the "online real-time monitoring-offline in-depth analysis" dual-detection system, and typical applications in disease modeling, biomarker screening, drug toxicity evaluation, and personalized diagnosis. It further explores Multi-Organ-Chip (MOC) systems and Artificial Intelligence (AI) empowerment, analyzes core bottlenecks including insufficient physiological complexity, lack of standardization, and barriers to clinical translation and industrialization, and prospects future directions from technological optimization, standardization establishment, and regulatory pathway exploration. By focusing on the IVD-oriented perspective, this review aims to provide theoretical references and practical guidance for the transformation of OoC from laboratory research to clinical IVD tools.
authors: Po Hao; Jingrong Deng; Jian Xu

title: A LITERATURE REVIEW OF RADIAL BASIS FUNCTION NEURAL NETWORKS FOR BLAST EXPLOSIVE PREDICTION
abstract: This review paper examines the development and application of Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN) for predicting blast explosive effects. Addressing the complexities of nonlinear and multi-physics blast phenomena, it highlights the advantages of data-driven approaches over traditional analytical methods. The paper presents the fundamentals of RBF networks, including their architecture, training techniques, and optimization strategies, emphasizing their capacity for universal function approximation and adaptability. A broad range of application domains such as mechanical control systems, energy and environmental modelling, medical diagnostics, and materials science underscore the versatility of RBF models. Performance evaluations demonstrate their robustness and accuracy in handling nonlinearities and uncertainties, although challenges related to computational complexity and data limitations persist. The review discusses hybrid modelling approaches and emerging methodologies like quantum kernels and interpretable artificial intelligence to address existing gaps. Ultimately, this synthesis underscores the significant potential of RBF neural networks in advancing blast effect prediction and suggests pathways for future research integrating novel computational techniques to further enhance prediction accuracy and reliability.
authors: Fakroul Ridzuan Hashim; Muhamad Izzuddin Abd Rahman; Kamsani Kamal; Mohd Fauzy Mohd Nor; Mohammed Alias Yusof; Suwimol Jungjit

title: Natural Language Processing for Real-Time Semantic Correlation of Shared Cyber Threat Indicators in National Defense
abstract: Defense intelligence systems receive continuous streams of natural-language threat reports in which the same event is frequently described using different terminology, structure, and coded language. Traditional keyword systems classify such reports as unrelated, fragmenting the intelligence picture and delaying coordinated response. This paper examines how Natural Language Processing (NLP) enables the real-time semantic correlation of shared cyber threat indicators. It reviews the progression from term-weighting and word embeddings to contextual transformer representations, and specifies an NLP pipeline that combines semantic encoding, similarity scoring, named-entity and relationship extraction, and clustering to link related threats into unified, analyst-ready groups. Using representative open-source and synthetic corpora, the study shows conceptually and through illustrative results that embedding-based correlation recognizes semantically equivalent reports that share few surface tokens, thereby exposing coordinated and evolving threats. The paper contributes a structured account of semantic correlation for defense CTI, a categorization of similarity thresholds into actionable intelligence bands, and a discussion of the operational and ethical conditions for deployment. The evaluation is illustrative rather than comparative: the behavior described and the similarity bands reported are indicative defaults presented together with a specified evaluation protocol and calibration procedure, not measured results, and the relationship of this work to the first author's earlier study of semantic correlation and de-duplication is disclosed and delineated explicitly. Subject to those qualifications, the findings suggest that NLP-driven correlation materially improves situational awareness and the speed of national defense response.
authors: Chukwunenye Amadi; Abolaji Adebayo; Ayokunle Olamide Ijagbemi
venue: Global Journal of Engineering and Technology Research

title: Opportunities and Challenges of Generative AI for Cybersecurity in Sub-Saharan African Organizations: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Generative AI (GAI) is increasingly used and studied across various fields in different countries; however, its implications for cybersecurity in Africa remain underexplored. This study investigates the opportunities and challenges of GAI on cybersecurity within the Sub-Saharan African organizations through a systematic literature review. Peer-reviewed journal articles and conference proceedings papers were retrieved from five databases, yielding 51 relevant publications, which were synthesized. The literature review was guided by the PRISMA flow diagram to ensure a structured review. Thematic analysis informed a taxonomy of GAI-related challenges and opportunities, aligned with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0. Key challenges include the absence of context-specific governance frameworks, technical and model-related limitations, data quality issues and people-related challenges. It was found that the reliance of GAI models on a few dominant languages limits their effectiveness in cybersecurity tasks such as threat detection within Sub-Saharan Africa’s multilingual context. Conversely, GAI presents opportunities to mitigate the region’s cybersecurity skills shortage by automating functions such as cybersecurity awareness and training, log analysis and continuous auditing. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers, practitioners, and governments seeking to harness GAI for cybersecurity in Sub-Saharan Africa, while also highlighting avenues for future research.

title: Development and validation of a dual-modal predictive model combining CT radiomics and clinical factors for adjacent vertebral refracture after PVP/PKP
abstract: Objective To establish a dual-modal predictive model combining CT radiomics and clinical factors for adjacent vertebral fractures (AVF) after percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) or percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP), and to validate its predictive performance. Methods A total of 348 elderly patients with osteoporotic thoracolumbar compression fractures (OTLCF) who underwent PVP/PKP at The First Affiliated Hospital of Lishui University (Lishui People’s Hospital) between May 2023 and November 2024 and completed a 6-month postoperative follow-up were enrolled as the training cohort. According to the occurrence of adjacent vertebral fracture (AVF) within 6 months after surgery, patients were classified into the AVF group (n = 68) and the non-AVF group (n = 280). A temporal validation cohort consisting of 149 patients treated at the same hospital between December 2024 and May 2025 was used to validate the predictive performance of the model, including 28 patients with AVF and 121 without AVF. Clinical characteristics were compared between the two groups. Radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics 3.0.1 and screened using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), analysis of variance (ANOVA), Pearson or Spearman correlation analysis, and the variance inflation factor (VIF). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative AVF after PVP/PKP. A nomogram for predicting AVF was constructed using R software. The predictive performance of the model was evaluated in both the training and temporal validation cohorts using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results The AVF group showed a significantly higher prevalence of diabetes, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ≥ 3 vertebral fractures, preoperative kyphotic deformity, lower bone mineral density, lower vitamin D levels, and poorer adherence to anti-osteoporosis treatment compared with the non-AVF group (all P < 0.05). Radiomics feature selection identified 10 independent predictive CT features: vertebral volume (Volume), first-order features including mean intensity (Mean), standard deviation (Std), and kurtosis (Kurtosis); and texture features including gray level co-occurrence matrix correlation (GLCM-Correlation), gray level run length matrix long-run emphasis (GLRLM-LRE), gray level size zone matrix zone size mean (GLSZM-ZSMean), gray level dependence matrix difference entropy (GLDM-DE), GLCM entropy (GLCM-Entropy), and GLRLM short-run emphasis (GLRLM-SRE). The radiomics score (Rad-Score) was calculated as follows: Rad-Score = 0.028 × Volume − 0.035 ×Mean + 0.041 × Std − 0.022 ×Kurtosis − 0.039 × GLCM-Correlation − 0.025 × GLRLM-LRE − 0.032 × GLSZM-ZSMean + 0.019 × GLDM-DE + 0.027 × GLCM-Entropy + 0.030 × GLRLM-SRE. Multivariate logistic regression revealed that ≥ 3 vertebral fractures (OR = 4.591, 95% CI: 2.330–9.045), preoperative kyphotic deformity (OR = 4.000, 95% CI: 2.099–7.623), bone mineral density (OR = 0.056, 95% CI: 0.015–0.200), good adherence to anti-osteoporosis treatment (OR = 0.184, 95% CI: 0.086–0.393), and Rad-Score (OR = 7.909, 95% CI: 1.914–32.691) were independent predictors of AVF after PVP/PKP (all P < 0.05). The nomogram achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.886 (95% CI: 0.845–0.927) in the training cohort, with a sensitivity of 82.35%, a specificity of 80.00%, and an optimal cutoff value of 0.723, demonstrating good discrimination between patients at high and low risk. Calibration analysis indicated good model fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow χ 2 = 6.892, P = 0.550; Brier score = 0.119). DCA showed that the model provided greater net benefit than either the treat-all or treat-none strategy across threshold probabilities ranging from 2% to 99%. In the temporal validation cohort, the model achieved an AUC of 0.877 (95% CI: 0.809–0.946), with a sensitivity of 82.14%, a specificity of 79.33%, and an optimal cutoff value of 0.721. Calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow χ 2 = 7.235, P = 0.510; Brier score = 0.121) and DCA demonstrated the model’s stability and potential clinical utility. Conclusion ≥ 3 vertebral fractures, preoperative kyphotic deformity, bone mineral density, good adherence to anti-osteoporosis treatment, and CT radiomics Rad-Score are associated with adjacent vertebral fractures after PVP/PKP. The predictive model based on these factors demonstrates high accuracy, good calibration, and clinical utility, providing an objective, quantitative, and convenient tool for assessing the risk of adjacent vertebral fracture. However, its generalizability across centers still requires further validation in multicenter cohorts.
authors: Wei Gan; Roulin Zhu; Guopeng Cui

title: Biosensors for Food Safety and Adulteration Monitoring: Applications, Smart Packaging Integration, and Pathways to Intelligent, Field‐Deployable Detection Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Food safety and authenticity remain major global public health concerns, necessitating rapid, sensitive, and cost‐effective analytical tools. This review critically evaluates recent advances in biosensing technologies for food safety monitoring, food adulteration detection, smart packaging, and data‐driven digital biosensing, providing an integrated perspective beyond the scope of previous reviews. Electrochemical, optical, and piezoelectric biosensors demonstrate remarkable analytical performance, enabling sub‐CFU pathogen detection and ppb‐level quantification of chemical contaminants across diverse food matrices, including milk, meat, seafood, cereals, and edible oils. Integration with smart packaging, such as colorimetric freshness indicators, pH‐responsive films, and on‐package contamination sensors, enables real‐time, non‐destructive quality assessment without conventional laboratory infrastructure. Furthermore, the convergence of biosensors with the Internet of Things (IoT), smartphone‐based imaging, machine learning, and cloud computing has accelerated the development of intelligent, connected food safety monitoring systems. Despite these advances, challenges related to matrix effects, long‐term stability, scalability, commercialization, standardization, and regulatory approval continue to hinder widespread implementation. This review critically discusses these limitations while highlighting commercialization strategies, technology readiness, and future research directions, including microfluidic integration, biodegradable sensing materials, explainable artificial intelligence, and blockchain‐enabled traceability, to support the development of reliable, scalable, and globally deployable food safety monitoring systems.
authors: Mohima Akther Any; Abid Hassan Arnab; Liza Akter; Yusuf Chowdhury; Md. Hassan Bin Nabi; Md Abu Rayhan; Nazmul Islam; Wahidu Zzaman

title: Diagnostic performance of ChatGPT for acute appendicitis compared with the Alvarado score: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
abstract: Acute appendicitis remains the most common cause of acute abdomen and is associated with serious complications such as perforation if not diagnosed promptly. While laboratory tests and clinical findings are essential, their interpretation can be challenging and sometimes misleading. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, has shown promise in supporting clinical decision-making and enhancing diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of ChatGPT-5 to predict the likelihood of appendicitis using clinical data, with diagnoses confirmed by histopathology and comparing it to Alvarado score which is most commonly known clinical scoring system to diagnose acute appendicitis. This retrospective comparative study evaluated the performance of ChatGPT-5 in predicting acute appendicitis across two phases. In Phase 1, the model was tested without prior context learning (i.e., without exposure to any previously labeled cases) to simulate real-world use of readily available LLMs. In Phase 2, it was re-tested after exposure to confirmed case outcomes. A structured prompting strategy was applied, incorporating patient demographics, clinical symptoms, laboratory data, and clinical context, with fixed output constraints across all cases. The dataset was divided into 70% (114 cases) for Phase 1 evaluation and 30% (48 cases) for Phase 2 validation. To address potential order leakage- a bias arising when predictions depend on case sequence rather than clinical reasoning- the cases were assessed both with and without randomization. Paired comparisons of sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy between ChatGPT-5 and the Alvarado score were performed using McNemar’s test, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess agreement. In Phase 1, ChatGPT-5 without randomization achieved a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 81.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 91.6%, negative predictive value (NPV) of 100%, and overall accuracy of 93.9%, compared with the Alvarado score (sensitivity 67.1%, specificity 92.1%, PPV 94.4%, NPV 58.3%, accuracy 75.4%). In Phase 2, ChatGPT-5 without randomization reached a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 93.8%, PPV of 97.0%, NPV of 100%, and accuracy of 97.9%, comparable to the Alvarado score (sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 93.8%, PPV 96.9%, NPV 93.8%, accuracy 95.8%). Within this retrospective, surgically confirmed cohort with a high clinical suspicion of acute appendicitis, ChatGPT-5 showed high diagnostic sensitivity for excluding acute appendicitis when guided by an optimized prompt, even without prior context learning. Proper randomization of prompt data appears essential to minimize order leakage and to provide a more conservative and reliable estimate of model performance. ChatGPT-5 cannot yet be relied upon to confirm acute appendicitis, given the higher specificity of the Alvarado score, and its diagnostic sensitivity remained largely unaffected by context learning, with only a modest, non-significant gain in specificity. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation in a broader emergency-department population before any clinical implementation.
authors: Amr A. Elgharib; Moustafa I. Ghanem; Rawan S. Ibrahim; Nour Elwakeel; Ayman Shemes

title: Plasma protein glycation, oxidation and nitration markers for improved risk prediction of Type 1 diabetes mellitus
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is characterized by hyperglycaemia caused by a deficiency of insulin resulting from autoimmune destruction of insulin-secreting beta cells of the pancreas. T1DM is caused by interaction of complex-trait genetic factors and environmental triggers such as viruses, endotoxin and possibly dietary effects. Recent studies have suggested that increased serum protein content of an advanced glycation endproduct is associated with increased risk of T1DM and also, with increased risk of cardiovascular disease in T1DM patients. The aim of this study is to quantify levels of Nε-Carboxymethyl-lysine (CML), other glycation endproducts, oxidation and nitration adducts in serum protein, in addition to related serum free adducts and amino acid metabolomics of monozygotic twins discordant for T1DM, and T1DM patients with HDL of high and low HAE, and compare these with plasma from healthy subjects. HDL apoA-1 exchange (HAE) – a measure of its ability to release lipid-poor apolipoproteinA-1, an essential step in reverse cholesterol transport. Monozygotic twins discordant for T1DM were studied from a London cohort and studies of T1DM patients with HDL of high and low HAE were based on an Oslo cohort. Major chemically-defined markers of protein damage by glycation, oxidation, and nitration were quantified in samples of plasma protein and in ultrafiltrate (glycated, oxidized and nitrated amino acids) by stable isotopic dilution analysis liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. In monozygotic twins there were increased protein glycation and oxidation markers in plasma and decreased nitration markers of plasma protein for the diabetic twin. However, increased nitration was observed in the second cohort of diabetic twins. In T1DM patients with HDL of high and low HAE, there were increased levels of glycation, oxidation and nitration of plasma protein in both patients groups with HDL of high and low HAE activity. There were changes in the amino acid metabolome in plasma of diabetic patients. This study reveals that dicarbonyl stress is a potential contributory impairment in T1DM and thereby very likely contributes to risk of CVD. Measurement of protein glycation, oxidation and nitration markers provides evidence of protein damage in healthy and patients with T1DM and also provides additional facility in the prediction for developing specific complications of metabolic disease.

title: POSTOPER ATIVE COMPLICATIONS AFTER COLORECTAL CANCER SURGERY: RISK FACTORS, IMPACT ON SURVIVAL, AND CONTEMPORARY PREVENTION STRATEGIES (A LITERATURE REVIEW)
abstract: Relevance: Postoperative complications remain major determinants of unfavorable outcomes following colorectal cancer surgery, contributing to increased mortality, reoperation rates, disease recurrence, and reduced long-term survival.The study aimed to analyze current evidence on postoperative complications after colorectal cancer surgery, identify major risk factors, evaluate their impact on long-term survival, and summarize contemporary preventive strategies.Materials and Methods: This structured literature review covered 39 publications from January 1, 2021, through July 31, 2026, including 34 original studies and 4 systematic reviews or meta-analyses; the GLOBOCAN 2022 fact sheet was used only for epidemiological context and was not counted among the included studies.Results: Reported overall postoperative morbidity ranged from 8.1% to 33.3%, while colorectal anastomotic leakage occurred in 4.7% to 15.1% of patients. Wen et al. reported postoperative infectious complications in 95/593 patients (16.0%), including wound infection, anastomotic leakage, intra-abdominal infection, pneumonia, and other infectious events. Severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grades III-V) occurred in 9.7-29.7% of patients. Significant adjusted associations included sarcopenia and postoperative complications (OR = 2.53; 95% CI: 1.45-4.42), three or more linear stapler firings and anastomotic leakage (OR = 2.71; 95% CI: 1.17-6.26), and male sex in a CT-based leakage model (OR = 3.75). In one colon cancer cohort, postoperative complications were associated with a higher adjusted risk of death (HR = 1.70; 95% CI: 1.19-2.45). Multimodal prehabilitation reduced major complications from 29.7% to 17.1%, while diverting ileostomy was associated with fewer leakage-related reoperations.Conclusion: Postoperative complications are consistently associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes following colorectal cancer surgery. Adjusted analyses identify nutritional, metabolic, patient-related, and technical factors that may support risk stratification. Multimodal prehabilitation, nutritional optimization, structured perioperative pathways, meticulous anastomotic technique, and selective diversion may reduce postoperative morbidity; however, the predominantly observational and heterogeneous evidence does not establish causality.
authors: Y. Zheldibaev; Aman Berkinbay; A. Aitakyn; D. Nurmakov; A. Raimkhanov; D. Zhumatayev

title: Artificial intelligence and laboratory biomarkers in veterinary medicine: an update about machine learning applications
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence has been a revolution in human medicine in the last years. Machine learning (ML), a subset of artificial intelligence, has allowed the use of a large amount of data to search for associations of clinical significance. Although the use of ML with laboratory biomarkers in veterinary medicine is limited in comparison with the human side, the number of studies published in this field is increasing in recent years. This review addresses some basic concepts and gives a general overview of the use of ML in the area of biomarkers in veterinary medicine. It is especially focused on two species of each companion (dogs and cats) and farm (bovine and porcine) animals, and provides information about the advances made in the last years, indicating how ML using laboratory data can contribute to the diagnosis and monitoring of selected diseases and, in case of farm animals, also to better control and improve their productive performance. In addition, possible new applications such as optimizing laboratory management, refining diagnostics or improving treatment monitoring based on the experience in humans are outlined. This narrative review can contribute to a better knowledge about the possible use of ML in laboratory biomarkers in veterinary and animal sciences for current and future applications.
authors: Fernando Tecles; Julián J. Árense-Gonzalo; Alberto Muñoz-Prieto; Asta Tvarijonaviciute; Silvia Martı́nez-Subiela; Edgar García Manzanilla; J. M. Castro Cerón

title: Implementation of next-generation sequencing to guide care and public health action in settings with high burden of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis: 32 stakeholder consensus statements generated using Delphi principles
abstract: Background: Comprehensive knowledge of resistance to the novel all-oral regimens for treatment of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) is important, but challenging variant detection by next-generation sequencing (NGS) in combination with variant interpretation software can diagnose resistance early. We aimed to generate a consensus on strategic issues for the implementation of NGS for routine RR-TB care. Methods: We employed a stakeholder consensus process informed by Delphi principles. First, stakeholders participated in an online survey to provide feedback on statements using a 3-point Likert scale and free text. Responses were then summarised and follow-up discussion fora with stakeholders were held to revise statements until a consensus was reached. Findings: Of the 116 invited stakeholders, 58 participated, representing RR-TB research (n=28), clinical care (n=11), diagnosis (n=5), RR-TB survivors and advocacy communities (n=5) from 14 countries in five of the six WHO regions. A consensus was rapidly reached for most statements with limited editorial changes needed. The debate mostly focused on statements covering performing sequencing at centralised facilities, acting on variants without statistical association with resistance in the WHO catalogue of mutations, strengthening WHO-endorsed regimens and the need for informed consent for the use of NGS for care and surveillance. Interpretation: The consensus-building process grounded in real-world experience from a diverse group of stakeholders generated 32 consensus statements covering five strategic domains. The blueprint generated is not a definite prescriptive framework but a document that can support policymakers when developing country-specific policies for NGS-guided precision medicine and RR-TB care. Sources of funding: This work was supported by the Global Health EDCTP3 Joint Undertaking and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation under the GenPath Africa project (101103171), the Research Foundation Flanders (FWO) Odysseus (G0F8316N) and TBM grants (T001018N).

title: Recent Advances in Sample Preparation for Cholesterol and Oxysterol Analysis in Complex Biological Matrices
abstract: Cholesterol and oxysterols are key molecules that regulate physiological processes and participate in the occurrence and progression of various major diseases. Accurate and efficient analytical detection of these substances in complex biological matrices is critical for disease mechanism research and biomarker discovery. However, challenges including complex biological matrices, large differences in analyte abundance, susceptibility to auto‑oxidation, low ionization efficiency, and difficulty in isomer separation pose severe obstacles to reliable analysis, making sample preparation the core step for accurate quantification and valid identification. Continuous innovations have been achieved in sample preparation techniques, such as liquid-liquid extraction, solid‑phase extraction, deep eutectic solvent extraction, molecularly imprinted extraction, derivatization, as well as integrated and automated workflows. These advances improve extraction efficiency, selectivity, antioxidant protection, and throughput, while effectively reducing matrix interference and artificial oxidation. This paper systematically reviews the research progress in sample preparation for cholesterol and oxysterol analysis in complex biological matrices from 2015 to 2026, highlights the technical advantages, application scenarios, and current limitations of various pretreatment strategies, and prospects the development trends toward greening, intelligence, and high throughput.
authors: Haizhen Zhang; Longchan Liu; Haoyue Zhang; Linnan Li; Zhengtao Wang; Li Yang

title: Optimized surgical treatment and study management for oncology patients in East Saxony (MISSION4Sax): study protocol of a multicentre pilot study
abstract: PURPOSE: MISSION4Sax aims to develop and pilot new concepts for cross-sectoral oncological care, data integration and networking between maximum care centres and rural practitioners in medical underserved, enabling access to guideline-based therapy, innovative surgery, and clinical trials. METHODS: This pilot project is an exploratory multicentre, prospective longitudinal study. It assesses the feasibility, acceptability, implementation and data-quality aspects of the proposed care model and study infrastructure, rather than to determine the effectiveness or causal impact of the interventions. It implements an interdisciplinary, cross-sectoral care model centred on a regional surgical indication tumour board at the National Center for Tumor Diseases (NCT) Dresden. Evidence-based, standardised patient care pathways are developed and piloted across three regional hospitals and two oncology practices. A database using the infrastructure of the NCT Core Unit "Registry Trial Platform", targeted training programmes and "Flying Data Nurses" support coordination, data flow and communication. Patient-reported outcomes complement the clinical data. Routinely collected health insurance data will be used exclusively as external reference data for a descriptive comparison with the MISSION4Sax cohort; no individual-level data linkage will be performed. A mixed-methods process evaluation will be performed alongside the project. EXPECTED OUTCOMES: The study will assess feasibility in routine care and explore access to specialised care, waiting times, coordination, pathway adherence, and clinical and patient-reported outcomes. CONCLUSION: Strengthening cancer care infrastructure, interdisciplinary cooperation, and digital systems may support equitable access to high-value care in rural regions. The proposed tumour board, patient pathways, and trained staff may improve care quality and collaboration across sectors. TRIAL REGISTRATION: DRKS00036134 (registration date: 30 June 2025).

title: Influence of Vitamin D-Based Oral Rinses on Salivary Diagnostics: Clinical and Research Considerations for Viral Detection and Oral Health
abstract: Saliva has gained increasing attention as a noninvasive diagnostic tool in both oral and systemic health. Its ease of collection, patient acceptability, and potential to reflect underlying physiological and pathological processes have supported its growing use in clinical and research settings. In the context of viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, saliva has been explored as an alternative to conventional nasopharyngeal sampling, offering a more accessible approach to detection. However, the reliability of saliva-based diagnostics may be influenced by preanalytical factors that remain underrecognized, highlighting the importance of considering oral interventions as potential preanalytical variables in salivary diagnostics while also creating opportunities for future therapeutic applications. From a clinician-researcher perspective, particular attention must be given to the oral environment and its dynamic nature. Interventions such as oral rinsing may alter the composition of saliva and consequently affect diagnostic outcomes. Observations from clinical work suggest that while oral rinsing may reduce antigen detectability in saliva, it does not necessarily correspond to a reduction in viral RNA levels, raising important considerations regarding the interpretation of test results. These considerations are particularly relevant when saliva is used for clinical testing, as variations in oral conditions and sample preparation may influence the measured diagnostic signal. Understanding these factors may help clinicians and researchers interpret salivary findings more appropriately and recognize the limitations of test results. Further attention to standardized collection procedures and the timing of oral interventions may therefore improve consistency and support more reliable application of saliva-based diagnostics across clinical and research settings in future.
authors: Sarah M. Nizar Feteih

title: Scientific and methodological foundations for teaching physicochemical analysis methods in continuous chemical education: a scoping review
abstract: Background Rapid technological advancement, digitalization of analytical instrumentation, and the growing demand for interdisciplinary competence have significantly transformed the role of analytical chemistry in science and industry. These changes necessitate a systematic reconsideration of how physicochemical analysis methods are taught within continuous chemical education. Objective This scoping review aimed to map and systematize the structural components of modern analytical chemistry education, identify dominant pedagogical approaches, and conceptualize their functional interrelationships within an integrated educational framework. Design/methods The study was conducted as a scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search was performed in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ACS Publications, SpringerLink, and RSCI (eLIBRARY.ru), covering publications from 1975 (the earliest eligible record retrieved) to 2024. Eligible studies addressed pedagogical, curricular, or methodological aspects of teaching analytical chemistry or physicochemical analysis methods. Extracted data were analyzed using qualitative thematic synthesis and conceptual mapping to identify recurring educational components and trends. Results The analysis revealed a consistent shift from method-centered instruction toward competence-oriented and system-based educational models. The most frequently reported components included integration of theoretical principles with laboratory practice, problem-based and research-oriented learning, incorporation of digital tools and chemometrics, emphasis on metrology and data interpretation, and increasing attention to sustainability and green analytical chemistry. The evidence indicates a transition from isolated presentation of analytical techniques to structured training focused on analytical thinking, decision-making, and interpretation of complex data. Conclusions Modern analytical chemistry education is evolving toward an integrated, interdisciplinary, and competence-driven model that prioritizes conceptual understanding, information processing, and real-world problem solving. The structural framework identified in this review may support curriculum development, modernization of laboratory courses, and alignment of educational programs with contemporary scientific and industrial demands.
authors: A. B. Toibazarova; K. Sh. Arynova; N. S. Zhussupbekova; E. A. Nazarov; G. T. Balykbayeva; A. T. Shuragaziyeva; Ж. К. Куанышева; N. O. Appazov

title: AI-facilitated analytical chemistry technologies: Advancing liquid biopsy for early cancer detection
abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and many solid malignancies are still diagnosed at advanced stages, when curative-intent therapies are less feasible and prognosis is substantially poorer. This diagnostic gap underscores the need for sensitive, minimally invasive approaches to early tumor detection. As an emerging alternative to tissue biopsy, liquid biopsy enables minimally invasive analysis of tumor-derived circulating biomarkers, including circulating tumor cells, circulating tumor DNA, extracellular vesicles, proteins, and metabolites. Its compatibility with repeated sampling enables longitudinal application across early detection, recurrence monitoring, prognostic assessment, and precision oncology. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with analytical chemistry technologies, including solid-phase microextraction, spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, electrochemical sensing, and microfluidics, can improve the detection, interpretation, and clinical translation of liquid biopsy-derived molecular data. This review critically evaluates AI-assisted analytical chemistry approaches for liquid biopsy-based early cancer detection, with an emphasis on multi-omics analysis. Specifically, this review examines (1) the biological relevance of circulating biomarkers, (2) isolation, enrichment, separation, and detection methods across the pre-analytical and instrumental stages, and (3) the evolution of AI from machine learning-based classification toward deep learning-based representation learning, self-supervised and transformer-based modeling, and multimodal and foundation-model approaches for molecular signal recognition, multi-omics integration, cancer classification, and cancer signal origin prediction. Furthermore, it discusses applications in cancer detection, recurrence monitoring, and multi-cancer early detection (MCED), as well as treatment-response assessment and AI-assisted clinical decision support, together with challenges involving assay standardization, model interpretability, false-positive management, and prospective validation. This review aims to provide an integrated framework that bridges analytical chemistry and AI to support the clinical translation of AI-assisted liquid biopsy for early cancer detection.
authors: Shengdong Ran; Chunjie Shi; Wanyi Chen; Lixian Li; Janusz B. Pawliszyn

title: Group-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Heart Disease Prediction Using Optimized CatBoost
abstract: Accurate and reliable heart disease prediction can support early risk assessment and improve clinical decision-making. However, repeated or duplicate observations in widely used heart disease datasets can introduce data leakage and lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a duplicate-aware and explainable machine learning (ML) framework for heart disease prediction. A combined dataset containing 1,328 records and 13 clinical features was systematically analyzed, resulting in 605 unique feature groups. To enable reliableA classification model which can identify a decision boundary that maximize the separation between the two outcome classes was added to SVM, one of the kernel-based classification models evaluation, the feature groups were partitioned into 484 development groups and 121 independent test groups. Six ML models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were comparatively evaluated using five-fold group-aware stratified cross-validation. CatBoost achieved the highest mean ROC-AUC among the evaluated models and was subsequently optimized using the development data. The optimized CatBoost model achieved an accuracy of 88.64%, precision of 89.92%, recall of 87.22%, F1-score of 88.55%, and ROC-AUC of 93.32% on the independent test set containing 264 records. At the unique feature-group level, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.78%, precision of 90.91%, recall of 81.97%, F1-score of 86.21%, and ROC-AUC of 93.28%. SHAP-based explainability analysis identified chest pain type, thalassemia status, ST-segment slope, number of major vessels, and resting electrocardiographic characteristics as among the most influential clinical features. The findings demonstrate that combining duplicate-aware evaluation, optimized CatBoost modeling, independent group-level testing, and SHAP-based explainability can provide a more reliable, robust, and transparent framework for heart disease prediction.
authors: Romaan Khan; Tufail Ahmad khan; Muhammad Tahir; Habib Un Nabi; Waqar Saeed; Muhammad Khan
venue: International Journal of Innovations in Science and Technology

title: The Unbearable Lightness of Prompting. A Critical Reflection on the Environmental Impact of genAI use in Design Education
abstract: Design educators are finding ways to support students in skillfully using GenAI tools in their practices while encouraging the critical scrutiny of the ethical and social issues around these technologies. However, the issue of environmental sustainability remains unaddressed. There is a lack of resources to grasp the environmental costs of genAI in education, but also, and foremost, a lack of shared practices for engaging with the issue. This paper critically reflects on the energy costs of using genAI in design education, using a workshop held in 2023 with 49 students as a springboard for reflection. Through this reflection, we develop a set of five alternative stances: acceptance, shift, moderation, friction, and refusal. Each of these, and the related actions, can support a conscious use of genAI in design education. The work contributes to the field of design and HCI by bringing together ways for educators to reflect on their practices, informing the future development of educational programs around genAI.
authors: Maria Luce Lupetti; Elena Cavallin; Dave Murray-Rust

title: THE INTEGRATION OF TECHNOLOGIES OF NUCLEAR INDUSTRY INTO HEALTH CARE: THE ORGANIZATIONAL ECONOMICAL MECHANISM
abstract: The purpose of the study is to analyze organizational economical mechanism of integration of technologies of nuclear industry into health care. The methodology is based on systemic, institutional and intersectoral approaches using statistical and structural functional analysis. It is established that in Russia, in 2015-2025 volume of radionuclide therapy procedures increased more than twofold times (from 4-5 thousand to 13-15 thousand procedures annually). The number of centers of nuclear medicine reached 18-22. The percentage of state financing made up to 60%-70%, whereas deficiency of human resources reached 20%-30%. It is established that key limitations of integration are institutional barriers, high capital intensity of projects, regional differentiation of infrastructure. The scientific novelty is in development of organizational economic mechanism of integration of technologies of nuclear industry into health care as interdisciplinary system of interaction between industrial, scientific and medical sectors. The practical significance study results is associated with possibility to apply results under improvement of mechanisms of management of high-tech medical care.
authors: T. Yu. Dzholdosheva; A. B. Mottaeva; O. V. Suzeva; V. D. Petelina

title: Artificial Intelligence in Infection Prevention: From Prediction to Protection
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), first defined by John McCarthy in 1955, refers to the science of developing intelligent machines capable of performing tasks that traditionally require human reasoning, learning, and decision-making. Since its early development in the 1960s and rapid expansion in the 2000s, AI has evolved substantially, driven by the availability of large digital health datasets, advances in machine learning, and increased computational power. In infection prevention and control (IPC), AI is emerging as a powerful tool for strengthening surveillance, improving diagnostic accuracy, predicting outbreaks, and supporting timely clinical interventions. AI-powered systems can analyze electronic health records (EHRs), laboratory results, antimicrobial prescribing patterns, microbiological data, patient demographics, and real-time hospital surveillance information to identify patients at high risk of infection and detect potential healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) at an early stage. Furthermore, AI can support antimicrobial stewardship by identifying inappropriate prescribing patterns and predicting antimicrobial resistance trends. Integration of data from wearable devices, environmental sensors, imaging systems, and unstructured clinical notes can provide continuous, real-time monitoring of infectious diseases and infection risks. AI-enabled computer vision and sensor-based technologies may also facilitate automated hand hygiene monitoring, helping healthcare facilities improve compliance with infection-control practices. Predictive models can identify emerging clusters of infection and assist public health teams in forecasting potential outbreaks, enabling earlier containment measures. Thus, AI effectively bridges prediction and protection, enhancing patient safety, healthcare quality, and operational efficiency. However, successful implementation requires high-quality data, robust validation, privacy protection, ethical governance, transparency, and recognition of the limitations of correlation-based predictions.
authors: Madhumita Das

title: Preclinical evaluation of AL-001, a gene therapy for wet age-related macular degeneration
abstract: Background Frequent intravitreal administration of antivascular endothelial growth factor Vascular endothelial growth factor agents remains a major limitation in the management of wet age-related macular degeneration (wAMD). This study evaluated whether suprachoroidal delivery of an engineered recombinant adeno-associated viral (rAAV)-aflibercept vector could achieve sustained, targeted expression with improved efficacy and safety compared with intravitreal administration. Methods AL-001, an engineered rAAV vector expressing aflibercept, was developed and characterized. Its expression profile was first assessed in New Zealand white rabbits following suprachoroidal space (SCS) injection. Efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and safety were then evaluated in a nonhuman primate model of laser-induced choroidal neovascularization (CNV), comparing SCS and intravitreal (IVT) administration routes. Results AL-001 efficiently expressed aflibercept in relevant ocular cells in vitro . In rabbits, SCS administration produced sustained aflibercept levels in ocular tissues. In the nonhuman primate CNV model, a single SCS injection of AL-001 showed favorable efficacy to IVT injection and a notable mild inflammatory response. At week 4, grade IV lesion incidence was 0% (0/48) after SCS administration versus 14.3% (6/42) after IVT administration (absolute difference, −14.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 3.7%–27.8%; P = 0.0258). Throughout follow-up, mean leakage area and grade IV lesion incidence remained 0 with SCS, versus IVT peaks of approximately 0.3 mm 2 and 33.0%, respectively, declining to 0.03 mm 2 and 2.0% by day 100. Both the medium and high doses decreased pathological vascular leakage and subretinal hyperreflective material. Vector administration preceded laser-induced CNV modeling, demonstrating that sustained intraocular aflibercept expression in the retina and choroid provided durable antiangiogenic protection. Pharmacokinetic analysis confirmed distinct ocular exposure profiles between routes, with viral genomes confined predominantly to the injected eye and no significant systemic accumulation. AL-001 was well tolerated, without sustained intraocular pressure elevation or severe ocular inflammation, and only mild-to-moderate treatment-emergent adverse events. Low pre-existing anti-AAV2 immunity and time-dependent neutralizing antibody responses postdosing, informing a translational model for patient stratification and redosing feasibility. Conclusion Suprachoroidal administration of AL-001 is well tolerated and provides durable, targeted aflibercept expression with pronounced antiangiogenic efficacy. These results support AL-001 as a promising, long-acting therapeutic candidate for wAMD.
authors: Xuan Liu; Haiyan Liu; Lei Wang; Zhao Julia; Xingwang Xie; Long Jiang; Chunlin Adam Zhao

title: Transfusion Science for Acute Surgical Emergencies
abstract: Transfusion science remains central to managing acute surgical hemorrhage. This review traces the evolution from early direct donor-to-recipient techniques to contemporary hemostatic resuscitation, noting a renewed emphasis on whole blood for severe hemorrhagic shock. Current practice employs a range of products – whole blood, red cells, plasma, platelets, cryoprecipitate, and fibrinogen concentrates – each with distinct physiologic roles and indications. We examine the development and implementation of massive transfusion protocols that prioritize early activation, multidisciplinary coordination, laboratory-guided resuscitation, and balanced product delivery to improve outcomes. Operational challenges – prehospital transfusion, austere-environment strategies (including walking blood banks), logistics, inventory management, and Rh compatibility – are addressed to highlight barriers to timely access. Finally, emerging innovations are reviewed, including improved hemorrhage-control techniques, freeze-dried plasma, cultured blood products, hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers, advanced molecular typing and universal-donor technologies, and AI-driven decision support and predictive logistics. Collectively, these advances underscore an evolving field committed to safer, more effective, and more accessible transfusion therapies across civilian, military, and resource-limited settings.
authors: Mary Stuever; Emmanouil Liodakis; Martin Schreiber; Jennifer Lynde; Omar Rokayak; Kelsey White; Jenny Guido; Lisa M. Angotti; Ronnie L Hill; Richard Tan

title: Primary Neoplasms of the Seminal Vesicles: A Narrative Review of Carcinoma and the Rarer Non-Epithelial and Biphasic Tumours
abstract: Primary carcinoma of the seminal vesicle is an exceptionally rare genitourinary malignancy, with evidence limited largely to case reports and small retrospective series. Diagnosis requires exclusion of more common secondary involvement from prostate, bladder, or rectal carcinoma through integration of clinical findings, imaging, histomorphology, and immunohistochemistry. Patients typically present with nonspecific symptoms and often have locally advanced disease. Computed tomography identifies retrovesical masses, while magnetic resonance imaging provides superior local staging. Core biopsy may establish the diagnosis, although definitive classification may require resection. The typical immunophenotype is CK7-positive, often with CA-125 expression, and negative for PSA, PAP, and NKX3.1; however, no marker profile is invariable. A contemporary panel including GATA3, p63/p40, uroplakin markers, CK20, p53, CD44, CDX2, and SATB2 is important for excluding urothelial and intestinal primaries. Conventional papillary adenocarcinoma is the predominant histological type, with mucinous, clear cell, squamous, and neuroendocrine variants also reported. Non-carcinomatous primary seminal vesicle neoplasms, including germ-cell tumours, sarcomas, solitary fibrous tumour, and mixed epithelial and stromal tumour, form an important differential diagnosis. Complete surgical excision with negative margins is the treatment most consistently associated with prolonged survival in the reported cases and is generally regarded as the only potentially curative option, whereas radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and hormonal therapy are selectively used for advanced or recurrent disease. International registries and collaborative molecular studies are needed to improve diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.
authors: Athanasios Zachariou; Grigorios Daligkaros; Μaria Filiponi
